name: Deepcore RadSkin Tunnel Worker Suit MK-2
description: Mottled grey-green with orange reflective banding, the RadSkin is a full-body soft-shell suit built for Shelf-level tunnel crews working contaminated substrata. The outer layer is bonded graphene-weave over a lead-flex membrane, visibly patched at the knees and elbows where previous owners added scrap ceramic tile reinforcement. Interior seams are sealed with pressure tape, yellowed from use. Wrist and ankle closures are ratchet-cinch rubber rings. The hood integrates a filtered face port with a cracked polycarbonate visor — often replaced with aftermarket lenses.
functionality: Provides moderate gamma and beta radiation shielding rated for contaminated zones up to 3.2 mSv/hr. Integrated boot cuffs seal against ground pooling. Not rated for alpha emitters without supplemental respirator. Patch-repair extends suit life but degrades shielding uniformity.
what_it_says: You work the deep tunnels, you breathe the bad air, and you don't expect anyone to replace your gear when it fails.
story_hooks: A cracked visor port has been repaired with layered bioadhesive — the previous owner's blood type is still printed on the collar tag.
Deepcore suits carry no serial numbers, making them untraceable — useful for crews working tunnels that officially don't exist.
A radiation exposure log stitched into the lining shows this suit has exceeded its safe lifetime by 400 hours.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian full-body suit with a distinctly lived-in, cobbled-together aesthetic. The silhouette is blocky and functional, designed for maximum coverage and mobility in confined spaces. The mottled grey-green base reads as industrial camouflage, while the orange reflective banding creates high-visibility striping along shoulders, torso, and limbs. The integrated hood gives it an almost hazmat appearance, but rougher, more street-level.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed but structured—roomy enough for layering and movement through tight tunnels, with reinforced panels at stress points. Not tailored; built for durability over fashion. Compression-fit at wrists and ankles via ratchet closures.
physical_description.primary_material: Bonded graphene-weave outer layer over lead-flex membrane. Sealed pressure-tape interior seams. Visible scrap ceramic tile patches at knees and elbows (user-applied reinforcement).
physical_description.texture: Rough, slightly waxy graphene surface with a subtle weave pattern. Pressure tape seams are visibly yellowed and slightly raised. Ceramic tile patches create hard, irregular geometry. Hood fabric is softer but shows creasing and staining from repeated use.
physical_description.color_scheme: Mottled grey-green base with burnt-orange reflective banding. Yellowed pressure tape adds beige-cream accents. Occasional rust stains and dirt patina throughout. The cracked polycarbonate visor has a milky, aged appearance.
physical_description.closures: Ratchet-cinch rubber rings at wrists and ankles. Hood visor is fixed to the frame. Interior sealing via pressure tape rather than traditional zippers (zippers would compromise containment).
distinctive_features: Integrated filtered face port with cracked polycarbonate visor (often swapped for aftermarket lenses)
Ceramic tile knee and elbow patches (scrap material, previous owner repairs)
Yellowed pressure-tape seams indicating heavy use
Lead-flex membrane visible at stress points and seams
Hood design extending coverage over upper torso
Ratchet-cinch closures designed for one-handed operation in gloves
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 salvage/sub-grade. Deepcore is a street label manufacturing shelf-level protective gear. This suit is built from reclaimed and recycled materials, patched with scrap, and worn by tunnel crews operating in ungoverned contaminated zones.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by Shelf-tier tunnel workers, scavengers, and hazmat cleanup crews operating in the GLMZ's deep infrastructure. Signals someone who works in brutal, high-risk conditions for minimal compensation. A badge of survival and grit, not status. The visible patches and age marks tell a story of multiple owners and countless hours in toxic environments.
physical_description.condition_typical: Weathered and well-patched. Never pristine—these suits accumulate damage, staining, and repairs. The visor cracks are normal; replacement is routine. Pressure tape seams yellow and fray with use. Ceramic patches collect chips and gaps. A 'good' one is simply one that still seals and doesn't leak.
